I don't have price data for today, so I can't tell you whether the stock moved up or down. However, the refining environment shows mixed signals. US crude is trading at $99.64 per barrel while Brent is around $107, and refineries are running at a healthy 94.5% capacity—conditions that typically support refiner margins. But crude prices have weakened over the past two days on hopes that the Iran conflict might ease, which reduces geopolitical risk premium and puts downward pressure on oil prices overall.

The conflicting signals from Washington matter here: Trump's comments about the Iran situation ending "fairly soon" pushed crude lower, but Secretary of State Rubio just said negotiations remain unproductive, which keeps uncertainty alive. For a refiner like this one, cheaper crude is a double-edged sword—it cuts into the value of refined products sold, while lower input costs help. Gasoline and diesel inventories are relatively healthy, which suggests steady demand but no supply crunch to drive prices up.
